To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the odor and taste profile in the cocoa beans from cultivated plants in Soconusco were evaluated by trained panellists.
the sensory descriptors of cocoa bean samples from cultivated trees of the Soconusco area in Chiapas, Mexico are sweet taste and sweet odor.

the sensory descriptors of cocoa beans are related to the quality and aroma of cocoa beans from trees cultivated in Soconusco region, and the sensory evaluation of cocoa beans from the region could be useful to identify the most appropriate samples for chocolate production.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the sensory quality of cocoa beans from trees cultivated in Soconusco region, Chiapas, México.
the characterization of sensory attributes in cocoa beans from Soconusco and their association with the origin of the sample.

the sensory evaluation of cocoa bean samples from trees cultivated in the southern part of Mexico, and the identification of the sensory descriptors that characterize them, as well as the identification of the samples with better sensory quality.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the cocoa bean samples from cultivated trees from the southern region of Mexico, evaluated in this study, showed a high degree of variability in their sensory characteristics, with some samples that could be considered of good quality, and others with sensory characteristics that could be improved.
samples with higher sweet taste and sweet/nutty odor, and lower off-odor and astringency are the best samples in terms of sensory quality.
G7 and G6 were the best quality cocoa beans, and G2 and G4 were the worst.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, in general, the sensory descriptors of the samples evaluated were in the expected range for cocoa beans, but the samples with better sensory quality were those with higher scores in the descriptors sweet and nutty, while samples with off-odor and/or musty odor were considered of poor quality.
there are cocoa beans from cultivated plants in the Soconusco area that have a sensory profile that is similar to that of cocoa beans from Theobroma cacao L. from other regions of the world.

the samples from the southern Mexican cocoa bean samples were grouped into seven groups according to their sensory profiles, and the samples with the most desirable sensory characteristics were those with the highest scores in the descriptors sweet and nutty, and with low scores in the descriptors off-odor and astringency.
The main takeaway from our work is that

it is possible to detect sensory differences between samples of cocoa beans from trees cultivated in the same region, which is of utmost importance to the development of new varieties with specific sensory characteristics.
the sensory descriptors of the cocoa bean can be used as quality parameters for the characterization of samples from the same origin, and to determine the quality of the cocoa bean.
the samples of cocoa from Chiapas, Mexico, are of good sensory quality and that it is possible to detect samples with high sensory scores.
